# Sirach Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_007_page_001.jpg

---

1 Do no evil, and no evil will overtake you.

2 Stay clear of wrong and it will stay clear of you.

3 Do not sow in the furrows of injustice, lest you reap them sevenfold.

4 Do not seek from the Lord a place of prominence, nor from the king a seat of honor.

5 Do not justify yourself before the Lord, nor try to seem wise before the king.

6 Do not seek to become a judge unless you have the strength to deal with injustice; otherwise you may show partiality to a powerful person and compromise your integrity.

7 Do not sin against the assembly of your city and do not disgrace yourself before the people.

8 Do not give yourself over to repeating a sin, for it is not without consequence even once.

9 Do not say, "He will take note of the many gifts I bring, and when I offer to the Most High God he will accept it."

10 Do not be halfhearted in your prayer, and do not neglect giving alms.

11 Do not mock a person who is bitter in spirit, for there is one who humbles and exalts.

12 Do not devise harm against your brother, nor against any friend or close neighbor.

13 Refuse to utter any form of lie, for the habit of lying leads to no good.

14 Do not speak at length in the assembly of elders, and do not repeat yourself in your prayers.

15 Do not shirk hard work, and do not despise farming, which the Most High established.

16 Do not count yourself among sinners' ranks — remember that wrath does not delay.

17 Humble yourself greatly, for the punishment of the ungodly is fire and worms.

18 Do not barter a friend for money, or a true brother for the gold of Ophir.

19 Do not dismiss a wife who is sensible and good — her worth is more than gold.

20 Do not ill-treat a servant who works faithfully, nor a hired worker who devotes himself fully.

21 Treat a wise servant as you would a close friend; do not withhold his freedom from him.

22 If you have livestock, attend to them; if they are productive, keep them.

23 If you have children, discipline them and train them from an early age.

24 If you have daughters, guard their purity, and do not show excessive leniency toward them.

25 Give a daughter in marriage and you complete a great undertaking — but give her to a sensible man.

26 If you have a wife, do not put her away; but do not trust yourself to a woman you resent.

27 Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget your mother's labor in bringing you to birth.

28 Remember that through them you came into existence; what could you give them that would repay what they have given you?

29 Fear the Lord with your whole soul, and hold his priests in reverence.

30 With all your strength, love your Maker, and do not neglect his ministers.

31 Fear the Lord and honor the priest; give him his portion as commanded: the firstfruits, the sin offering, the gift of the shoulder, the sacrifice of consecration, and the firstfruits of the holy offerings.

32 Extend your hand to the poor as well, so that your blessing may be complete.

33 Give graciously to all the living, and do not withhold your kindness even from the dead.

34 Do not hold back from those who weep; mourn with those who mourn.

35 Do not hesitate to visit the sick, for by such acts you will be loved.

36 In all that you do, keep your last end in mind, and you will never sin.
